result.reviewScopeSummary: Follow-up verification focused on F-06-001, the trailing-turnless newest-closed-turn shape, directly touched boundary decision code, directly touched tests, production-path audit terms, focused tests, story gate, and epic gate.

priorFindingStatuses.rationale: Resolved by code and test evidence. `advanceDecision` now stops before the last candidate with a non-null `turnId`, protecting the newest closed turn and any later turnless singleton. The added TC-5.2 test covers two closed turns followed by a trailing turnless singleton and asserts boundary remains before the newest closed turn. The prior production-path probe now passes with `boundary: 3`, `zoneTokens: 130`, and rows t1/order 3, t2/order 7, trailing null/order 10.

newFindings.title: Trailing-turnless protection creates an unresolved AC-5.3 landing-window exception
newFindings.evidence: AC-5.3 still says the advance lands in `[target, target + one turn)`. The new trailing-turnless TC-5.2 leg in `view-boundary-turn-end.test.ts` uses budgets 100/60 with groups t1=50, newest closed t2=45, trailing turnless=70, then expects boundary after t1 and `zoneTokens` 115. If the next protected turn is the newest closed turn, the AC window is `[60, 105)`, so the expected 115 is outside it. This is not a code failure in the quick fix; it exposes a product/spec ruling needed for the legal trailing-turnless shape because a scalar boundary cannot both skip the trailing singleton and preserve the newest closed turn. The story technical notes were changed to protect trailing turnless singletons after the newest closed turn, but the AC wording and tech-design.md Flow 5 still carry the general landing-window phrasing.
